reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the webinar urges viewers to sell and build their business using a time-limited 10% token benefit, claiming that more tokens mean more coins. It also promotes membership and accumulation-based incentives, including a sales threshold for a start-up bonus, free package codes, and a stated package benefit, alongside high reported leader earnings. The promotional setting additionally directs members to paid event tickets and requests identity documents with stated account deductions for translation; the available video evidence does not establish fulfillment, actual payments, victim loss, document misuse, or the economic value of the tokens and packages.

opening.argument: The broadcast presents conditional promotions rather than a guaranteed financial outcome. Eligibility depends on specific timing, sales volume, package-code accumulation, and account status: the start-up bonus requires “5,500 BV collected out of personal sales,” while package rewards require banking defined quantities of codes. It also expressly limits earlier package codes by an activation deadline and distinguishes pending, conditionally approved, and approved accounts. Those qualifications make the message a rules-and-conditions announcement, not a promise that every viewer will profit. The supplied material contains no stated guarantee of returns, fixed appreciation, or assured income; the strongest claims are promotional encouragement, whose economic outcome remains unestablished.

All OneCoin package codes of these purchases will be valid only until Saturday, April the 30th, this year.
you can continue to trade on the OneCoin exchange regardless of whether your status is PENDING, Conditionally Approved or Approved.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side treats “10% more tokens” and “more tokens equals more coins” as a guaranteed investment promise, but the first is a time-limited promotional quantity and the second is an assertion about the program’s internal relationship, not proof of a guaranteed monetary return. The cited package-code deadline establishes an expiration rule, not deception. Likewise, mentioning reported leader earnings does not itself promise that viewers will receive them. The opening also concedes that fulfillment, payments, losses, and token value are not established, leaving the alleged scam mechanism inferential.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Conditions do not neutralize the central inducement. The broadcast explicitly tells viewers to activate package codes before a deadline and links additional tokens to additional coins. A qualification rule can describe how to obtain the advertised benefit without making the underlying offer legitimate. The reported earnings are displayed in a promotional context and followed by a forward-looking question about where viewers will appear, while no evidence establishes that the advertised token accumulation has economic value.

opening.argument: The material can reasonably be read as a recurring company-information webinar covering several distinct subjects, rather than a single solicitation. It identifies itself as a “State of the Nation Broadcast,” gives operational guidance about acceptable proof-of-address documents and translation charges, reports upcoming events, discusses a direct-selling earnings ranking, and describes a foundation donation and scholarship. The visuals likewise separate “EVENTS,” “PROMOTIONS,” “BUSINESS OPERATIONS,” “NEWS,” and “ONE WORLD FOUNDATION.” That breadth is consistent with news, member education, and operational instruction. Promotional language appears within those segments, but the supplied evidence does not establish that the entire broadcast is a disguised promise of financial returns.

citations.quote: welcome to this week's State of the Nation Broadcast
We would like to remind you all that the acceptable documents for proof of address are a utility bill, gas, water, electric
Business at Home the global direct selling news and information organization keeps a running score on the reported earnings of leaders in the industry.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the program a broadcast or webinar does not change what it asks members to do. The cited operational material is secondary to direct instructions to sell, build the business, activate packages, and acquire more coins. The earnings segment is not neutral reporting when it asks where the viewer will appear on the prestigious listing. Separate news and foundation segments may exist, but they do not erase the viewer-facing package and token promotion.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The operational and news segments do not make the financial promotion educational. The program tells members to sell and build their business immediately, offers package-based rewards, and presents token accumulation as producing more coins. A broad format can still contain a scam solicitation as its central commercial mechanism. The foundation and event material are additional credibility-building content, not evidence that the token offer has value or that the sales incentives are ordinary education.

opening.argument: Much of the concrete offer is ordinary commerce and member administration. The event has listed bronze, silver, and gold ticket prices, with free-ticket conditions for Diamond members and bulk orders. The broadcast also explains proof-of-address requirements, rejected document types, translation charges for certain Chinese accounts, and how approved members may use a document-copy function. These are recognizable event-sales and account-verification activities. The record does not show a deposit being made, a guaranteed return, a downline-income promise, misuse of credentials, victim loss, or a completed transaction. Even the free package-code rules specify quantities and categories rather than guaranteeing profit.

citations.quote: There are three different categories of tickets, bronze at a hundred euro, silver at a hundred and fifty euro and gold at two hundred euro.
For Chinese members with approved accounts, do note that in the case your uploaded documents have been translated and you being charged 15 euros
you can continue to trade on the OneCoin exchange regardless of whether your status is PENDING, Conditionally Approved or Approved.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Ticket sales and KYC procedures are peripheral. The core promotion connects package activation to more tokens and more coins, then layers on package-code accumulation incentives and reported million-dollar earnings. Calling the event ordinary commerce does not account for that token mechanism. The absence of shown victim loss or completed payment is not exculpatory: promotional scam content need not document its victims on camera. Nor does a quantity rule make a financial offer an ordinary loyalty discount.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The offer is not merely tickets or account administration. Package codes are tied to packages, tokens, and coins, and the broadcast urges viewers to sell and build the business. Calling those incentives “ordinary” assumes the very legitimacy at issue. The KYC language also confirms that documents and account charges are part of the same member system, while nothing cited establishes that the coins, packages, or reported earnings deliver real economic value.
